To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the arterial wall of the SHR rat has a smaller total connective tissue content, but a larger relative cell content.

the passive mechanics of arteries of the SHR are stiffer, the active mechanics of SHR arteries are altered, the connective tissue of SHR arteries is less extensive, and the smooth muscle cells of the SHR arteries are different.
the passive wall mechanics are stiffer in arteries from the SHR than in those from WKY, while active wall stress is greater and occurs at smaller values of strain in SHR than WKY arteries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanical properties of arteries in the SHR and WKY.
the mechanisms by which hypertension alters the mechanics of the arterial wall.
the mechanisms by which the arterial wall is able to maintain its mechanical integrity and function in the face of elevated pressure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SHR arteries are stiffer and more compliant than the WKY arteries.

differences in the mechanics of arteries from SHR and WKY rats are due to differences in the properties of the connective tissues, differences in the relative amounts of connective tissue and smooth muscle, and differences in the properties and/or amount of smooth muscle.
the altered wall mechanics in the SHR are the result of a complex combination of factors, including the altered properties of both connective tissue and smooth muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SHR carotid and tail arterial wall has a smaller total connective tissue matrix and a smaller extracellular space, but a larger cell content.
the altered mechanics in the arterial walls of the SHR are related to differences in the properties of both the connective tissue and the smooth muscle cells.
the altered arterial wall mechanics of SHR arteries are due to differences in the properties of the extracellular matrix and smooth muscle cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the altered arterial wall mechanics in the SHR is due in large part to the differences in the extracellular matrix.
differences exist in the mechanics of the connective and contractile tissues of SHR arteries compared to WKY, and these differences may contribute to the increased stiffness of the SHR arterial wall.
the differences in arterial wall mechanics between SHR and WKY rats cannot be explained solely by differences in the properties of connective tissue.
